breakdown.headline: Chelsea 0–2 Spurs

verdict.text: Chances were even (0.74 xG to 0.47), so the win came down to finishing and fine margins.

style.label: Field tilt (share of passes in opposition half)
PPDA, estimated (opponent passes per Spurs defensive action; lower = harder press)
Long balls as share of accurate passes
Share of xG from set plays

howSpursPlayed: Spurs had 69.0% of the ball and 77.4% of the passing in the opposition half, against a season average of 60.9%.
They took 15 shots (4 on target) worth 0.74 xG, about 0.05 per shot; Chelsea had 7 shots worth 0.47 xG.
Momentum: Chelsea on top, 12–18'; Spurs on top, 19–35'; Spurs on top, 55–61'; Spurs on top, 76–90.5'.
In short: dominated the ball, pinned the opponent back, lots of low-quality shots, took players on.
sources: FPL Core Insights (FotMob match data): shots, minutes, momentum, team and player match stats
breakdown.label: Generated automatically after the match by fixed rules from the stored data. Interpretation is calculated, not an expert opinion.

setup.formationNote: Formation and positions as listed on ESPN's team sheet: the nominal shape, not a measured one.

summary: Spurs lined up in a 4-2-3-1 against Chelsea's 3-4-2-1 (2 changes from the Coventry City game, switching from 3-1-4-2).
Chances were even (0.74 xG to 0.47), so the win came down to finishing and fine margins.
Compared with their other league games, Spurs conceded less (0.47 xG vs 1.34 xG), had more of the ball (69% vs 60%), played higher up the pitch (77% vs 66%), went long more often (5.4% vs 3.3%).
Marmoush was the biggest attacking threat (0.30 xG + xA); Fernandes won the ball back most often (6 tackles won + interceptions).

phases.title: Build-up and possession

rows.label: Long balls, share of accurate passes

read: Spurs had 69% of the ball (season average 60%), completing 569 of 654 passes (87%).
77% of all passing in the opposition half was by Spurs (field tilt), above their usual 66%. They spent long spells camped in Chelsea's half.
65% of Spurs' accurate passes were in their own half (370 own half, 199 opposition half): a lot of circulation at the back before progressing.
Long balls made up 5.4% of accurate passes (well above the season's 3.3%), with 53% of long balls finding a teammate.

phases.title: Chance creation
read: 15 shots (4 on target) worth 0.74 xG, 0.05 per shot; the season average is 0.08 per shot, so the chances were lower quality than usual.
8 shots came from inside the box and 7 from outside (47% from distance).
Spurs created 1 big chance and missed 1 (season average 2.1).
27 touches in Chelsea's box, in line with the season average of 29; Chelsea had 17 in Spurs' box.
Where the xG came from: open play 0.52 (54%), fast breaks 0.00, set pieces 0.44. 7 of the shots came straight from a teammate's pass (assisted).

phases.title: Finishing
read: Spurs scored 2 from 0.74 xG: 1.3 more than the chances were worth.
Shots on target were worth 1.12 xGOT against 0.74 xG before the shot: the finishing placed shots better than average.

phases.title: Out of possession
read: PPDA (estimated): 3.7 Chelsea passes in their own half per Spurs defensive action; season average 4.4. Lower means a more aggressive press, so this was a more intense press than usual.
21 tackles won and 7 interceptions (season averages 17.6 and 7.9); 12 clearances and 2 blocks.
Duels: Spurs won 64, Chelsea 46 (58% for Spurs); 71% of aerial duels won.
Chelsea managed 7 shots worth 0.47 xG (Spurs usually concede 1.34 xG) and 0 big chances.

phases.title: Transitions and set pieces
read: Fast breaks: Spurs had 0 shots on the break (0.00 xG); Chelsea had 0 (0.00 xG), against a season average of 1.6 shots conceded on the break.
Set pieces: 5 Spurs shots (0.44 xG, 1 goal); Chelsea 1 (0.02 xG, 0 goals). Corners: 6–4.

flow: First half: 0.43 xG for, 0.22 against (0–0). Second half: 0.52 for, 0.21 against (2–0).
Spells on top (momentum index): Chelsea 12–18'; Spurs 19–35'; Spurs 55–61'; Spurs 76–90.5'.
77' Spurs goal: Penders from a corner (xG 0.21).
87' Spurs goal: Tel from open play (xG 0.04).
Chelsea played with ten men after Palmer's red card (80'); figures after that point reflect the numbers difference.
